name: 3I/ATLAS, the interstellar comet
note: Only the third object ever seen visiting our solar system from interstellar space. It was discovered in July 2025.

name: Barnard's Star
note: A red dwarf 6 light-years away. It crosses our sky faster than any other star.

name: Kapteyn's Star
note: A very old star about 13 light-years away, with the second-fastest motion across the sky.

name: Groombridge 1830
note: A star about 30 light-years away, one of the fastest-moving stars in our sky.

name: Lacaille 9352
note: A red dwarf about 10.7 light-years away in the southern sky.

name: Wolf 359
note: One of the closest stars to the Sun, about 7.9 light-years away.

name: Teegarden's Star
note: A small red dwarf 12.5 light-years away with Earth-sized planets.

name: WISE J184125.47+095436.5
note: A star that NASA's WISE telescope flagged as variable years earlier. Can SPHEREx see it change?

name: Pleiades
note: A young star cluster about 440 light-years away, wrapped in dust that reflects starlight.

name: Crab Nebula
note: The remains of a star that exploded and was seen from Earth in the year 1054.

name: Orion Nebula
note: A cloud 1,300 light-years away where new stars are forming.
